title: A local ring is henselian (idempotent lifting) iff simple roots of monic polynomials lift
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring. The following are equivalent: (i) $R$ is henselian in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], i.e. for every finite $R$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/\mathfrak mB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$; (ii) for every monic polynomial $f\in R[T]$ and every $a_0\in\kappa$ with $\overline f(a_0)=0$ and $\overline{f'}(a_0)\neq0$ (where $\overline f\in\kappa[T]$ is the reduction of $f$) there exists $a\in R$ with $f(a)=0$ and $a\bmod\mathfrak m=a_0$.

source.place: algebra.tex Definition Tag 04GF (definition-henselian; Section Tag 04GE: (ii) is Stacks' definition of a henselian local ring) and Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), (1)<=>(10) (every finite R-algebra is a finite product of local rings); more-algebra.tex Definition Tag 09XE (definition-henselian-pair) with the remark following it (for a local ring, (R,m) is a henselian pair iff R is henselian) and Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), (1)<=>(3) (idempotents of B/IB lift uniquely for finite B)

proof.text: Universe bookkeeping: transfer the assumed lifting property from ULift B to any finite R-algebra B in Type u. The algebra equivalence ULift B ≃ B induces an equivalence of quotients by the extended maximal ideal. Transport the residue idempotent upward, apply the hypothesis, and transport the resulting idempotent downward. Only existence is needed in this direction.

For a monic f, put S=AdjoinRoot f, finite over R by [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]. More generally suppose its reduction is a product g0*h0 of coprime monic polynomials. Choose Bezout coefficients a*g0+b*h0=1 and put p0=b*h0. Lift the coefficients of p0 to a polynomial p over R. Under the coefficient-reduction equivalence S/mS ≃ kappa[X]/(fbar), the class e0 of p is idempotent: p0^2-p0=-(a*b)*(g0*h0). This constructs the CRT idempotent without importing a separate CRT statement.

Apply the assumed lifting property to e0 to obtain an idempotent e in S. For q=g0 or h0, the canonical map S→AdjoinRoot q kills mS, because its restriction to R factors through the residue map. Apply its induced quotient map to the equality e mod mS=e0. The images of e are therefore 1 in AdjoinRoot g0 (by the Bezout identity) and 0 in AdjoinRoot h0.

The maximal ideal of R lies in the Jacobson radical, since every maximal ideal equals it. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-splitting-monic-factorization] to e and the two computed images, obtaining monic g,h with f=g*h and reductions g0,h0.

For a simple residue root a0, take g0=X-a0 and h0=fbar divByMonic (X-a0). Polynomial.mul_divByMonic_eq_iff_isRoot gives fbar=g0*h0, monicity of fbar and g0 gives monicity of h0, and Polynomial.isCoprime_of_is_root_of_eval_derivative_ne_zero gives coprimality. Step 4 lifts this factorization. Since reduction preserves the natural degree of a monic polynomial, g has degree one; hence g=X+C(g.coeff 0). Put a=-g.coeff 0. Evaluating f=g*h gives f(a)=0, and comparing constant coefficients in gbar=X-a0 gives residue(a)=a0.

Conversely, the given root-lifting condition yields HenselianLocalRing R by HenselianLocalRing.TFAE, hence HenselianRing R (maximalIdeal R). Every finite R-algebra is integral. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-integral-idempotent-lifting], in its recorded Lean signature Algebra.existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_of_henselianRing, to any finite B and any residue idempotent. It supplies exactly the unique idempotent lift required on the left side.

lean.statement: theorem idempotent_lifting_iff_monic_simple_root_lifting (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : (∀ (B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [Module.Finite R B], ∀ e₀ : B ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R B), IsIdempotentElem e₀ → ∃! e : B, IsIdempotentElem e ∧ Ideal.Quotient.mk ((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R B)) e = e₀) ↔ (∀ f : Polynomial R, f.Monic → ∀ a₀ : ResidueField R, Polynomial.aeval a₀ f = 0 → Polynomial.aeval a₀ f.derivative ≠ 0 → ∃ a : R, f.IsRoot a ∧ residue R a = a₀)
lean.note: The idempotent condition is spelled out inline, as directed by the lean.note of def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology; the other side spells out the residue-field condition of HenselianLocalRing.TFAE. No private henselian predicate is introduced.
